title: Config loading dies on a missing key
summary: operator[] in nlohmann/json creates a null for a missing key. Read required keys with at(), optional ones with value(), and test with contains().

turns.user: if config.json has no timeout_ms it dies with type must be number, but is null. want it optional

assistant.body: Got it. The cause is operator[] on a json that is not const. For a missing key it inserts a null element and returns it, and converting that null to int throws type_error. In other words, just reading the config changes j. The required host and port move to at(), which throws out_of_range naming the missing key. The optional timeout_ms goes through value() with a default.

turns.user: oh and read the cert path only when there's a tls block. plain otherwise

assistant.body: Note: testing with j["tls"].is_null() would create a null tls entry just by asking. contains() never creates a key. Add std::string cert_path to Config and read it like this.
